title: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
focus: Minkä maalainen asks what nationality someone is. Minkä maalainen sinä olet? — Olen suomalainen.
targetSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What nationality are you?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. Minkä maalainen asks what nationality someone is. The joined spelling minkämaalainen is also used. A nationality is not automatically the country where someone currently lives or the place they travelled from. The complete question means “What nationality are you”.
requiredSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question modifier (asks which item or group) + nationality being asked about + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question modifier (asks which item or group)
parts.formation: Minkä is the genitive form of mikä and remains unchanged in these descriptive question phrases.

parts.role: nationality being asked about
parts.formation: Maalainen follows minkä in this singular nationality question phrase.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the singular you-form olet: ole- + -t.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Minkä maalainen Anna on?”: choose “Anna is Estonian.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. An adjective is a word that describes a quality. Reply with a nationality word: Olen suomalainen (“I am Finnish”). Nationality words begin with a lower-case letter, unlike country names such as Suomi (“Finland”). Learn the taught nationality words; do not assume every country name takes the same ending. For these words -lainen/-läinen belongs to the nationality word, not to olla. The complete reply means “Anna is Estonian”.
